companyDescription: Independent contract engagement. Client and program under NDA. Designed, built and validated sandboxed, machine-graded evaluation environments that measure the offensive and defensive security capability of frontier large language models and agentic systems.
achievements: Authored tasks from real vulnerability material, containerized each task into a reproducible environment, defined an explicit grading contract, and ran each task against multiple models through an agent harness.
Validated that each task discriminates: a pass had to reflect the capability the task claims to measure, not partial progress, a leaked solution or a single fortunate trajectory.

Combined deterministic machine checks with semantic LLM-as-judge rubrics instead of final-answer matching, and separated identification failure from remediation failure as distinct measurable signals.
Designed tasks against contamination and leakage so results stay meaningful across model generations.
Analyzed full agent trajectories to locate where model capability actually stops.
Delivered a 40 to 50% test-coverage improvement on one task set.

Applied measurement methods in daily work: precision and recall, threshold calibration, precision-recall versus ROC selection, inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, ICC) and item response theory.

Worked at offensive depth on real CVE families: heap exploitation, tcache and safe-linking free-list poisoning, type confusion, ROP and JOP chaining, arbitrary read and write primitive construction, ASLR and PIE defeat, and sandbox escape.
